summary: The accepted replay stops at the source-selected default angry-god reaction: pray.c:angrygods() calls the already represented gods_angry() voice and then god_zaps_you(), while js/pray.js records god_zaps_you as unported. Port the whole lightning/disintegration helper and its fry_by_god helper, then wire the existing JS angrygods route. The separate C-only desecrate_altar caller has no JavaScript implementation or caller path and remains outside this case.

source.branch: After prayer_done() resolves an unforced too-soon prayer (p_type 0), gods_upset() increments anger and calls angrygods(). Its rn2(maxanger) result must be in the default arm (> 8) after the cap to 15; this case source-records rn2(15)=10. That arm calls gods_angry(resp_god), then god_zaps_you(resp_god), before angrygods() updates ublesscnt with rnz(300). In god_zaps_you(), an unswallowed hero without shock resistance reaches fry_by_god() for lightning; a surviving wizard then receives the not-deterred line, wide-angle disintegration, worn cloak destruction, and the disintegration fry path. The direct C desecrate_altar() caller is a distinct absent JS path.
callers: Production C route exercised: pray.c:dopray() installs prayer_done() as afternmv; allmain.c:unmul() invokes it after the three immobile turns; pray.c:prayer_done() p_type 0 calls gods_upset(), which reaches angrygods() default and god_zaps_you(). Existing JavaScript wiring is pray.js:dopray/prayer_done -> gods_upset -> angrygods; only the default helper call is missing.

Other direct C call: pray.c:desecrate_altar() calls god_zaps_you() after its own deity voice. There is no JavaScript desecrate_altar function or JS caller route in this base; this task records that separate source gap and does not invent the route.
dependencies: pray.c:godvoice and gods_angry supply the source-ordered line before the helper; the existing JS angrygods default already calls godvoice with that text.
mondata.c:Resists_Elem(), already ported in js/mondata.js, supplies the return values for C resists_elec()/resists_disint() macros; its return is used for swallowed-monster branches.
do_wear.c:disintegrate_arm(), already ported in js/do_wear.js, is called for worn armor in the same shield, cloak, suit, shirt order; C discards its return and relies on effects.

mon.c:xkilled(), end.c:done(), display.c:shieldeff(), muse.c:ureflects(), mondata.c:monstseesu()/monstunseesu(), sounds.c:SetVoice(), pline.c:verbalize(), and minion.c:summon_minion() have existing JS implementations used for corresponding effects.
